item.title: Chinese AI Chipmakers Poised to Gain From Beijing’s Tech Push
item.description: China’s AI chip designers are expecting bumper sales this earnings season off the back of Beijing’s push to get local firms to use homegrown components and reduce their reliance on American tech.

item.title: Copper Heads for Record Close in London on Tighter Global Market
item.description: Copper headed for a record close in London after strong gains fueled by signs of tighter supply across the global market.

item.title: Taiwan Pension Fund Will Tap Third-Party Managers for Stock Bets
item.description: Taiwan’s $49 billion public-sector pension fund is planning to allocate more assets to third-party managers to boost its exposure to global stock markets.

item.title: Global Funds Pile Back Into India IT Stocks After Selling for Months
item.description: Smaller IT firms fared better than their larger counterparts during the June quarter.

item.title: China Exports, Imports Post Double-Digit Gains as AI Lifts Trade
item.description: China’s exports and imports kept up a strong growth pace while moderating in July, as a global investment supercycle in artificial intelligence helped offset disruptions to trade from extreme weather.

item.title: China’s Solar Stocks Whipsawed by Domestic Policies, US Tariffs
item.description: Chinese solar stocks were whipsawed this week by a combination of domestic efforts to end below-cost sales and renewed tariff threats from the US.

item.title: Philippine Growth Disappoints at 2.3% as War, Graft Sap Demand
item.description: Philippine economic growth slowed dramatically in the second quarter, defying expectations of a pickup, as consumer spending slowed and investment shrank. The peso and stocks fell.

item.title: US Sale of Euros for Yen Intervention Blindsided Europe, FT Says
item.description: The US blindsided the European Central Bank last week with its historic currency intervention to help Japan, only informing its counterparts in Frankfurt after it sold euros to buy the yen, the Financial Times reported, citing several people familiar with the matter.

item.title: AI Data Center Group Firmus Draws $2 Billion From Coatue, Nvidia
item.description: AI data center company Firmus raised $2 billion in a funding round backed by Coatue Management, Nvidia Corp., Blackstone Inc. vehicles and Jane Street, the company said.

item.title: Trading Strategies ‘Buried Alive’ by India’s Rocky Stock Reform
item.description: For much of the first week of trading under India’s new auction system to set closing stock prices, traders were convinced that one of the most consequential market structure reforms in years was faltering.

item.title: SK Hynix Directs Chip Windfall Into Korean Corporate Bond Market
item.description: The AI boom has prompted global tech giants to raise billions issuing bonds, but for at least one major manufacturer the involvement in credit markets doesn’t stop there.

item.title: China Central Bank Adds Gold in Hong Kong to Support Trading Hub
item.description: China’s central bank is stockpiling more gold in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter, in a move that’s likely to support the city’s push to become a major bullion-trading hub.

item.title: Tencent AI Spending Key After Magnificent 7 Rout
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd.’s spending plans will draw investor scrutiny as investors cool on lavish outlays on artificial intelligence.

item.title: Anwar’s Daughter Takes Leave from Party Leadership Amid Setbacks
item.description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s daughter has sought to relinquish her role as deputy president of his party, more than a year after her election fueled accusations of nepotism and exposed deep divisions within the ruling coalition.

item.title: Fujifilm Declines Most on Record on Profit Miss, Spinoff Plan
item.description: Fujifilm Holdings Corp. shares fell by the most on record after the Japanese company reported weaker-than-projected quarterly results.

item.title: Mexico Arrests Ex-Governor Over 2014 Student Abduction Case
item.description: Mexican authorities detained a former governor over charges he concealed evidence in the more than decade-old abduction and presumed murder of dozens of students training to be teachers, one of the country’s most infamous criminal cases.

item.title: Yen Surrenders Nearly Half Its Gains from US-Japan Intervention
item.description: The yen is heading into the end of the week having surrendered nearly half of its intervention-driven gains, fueling speculation among traders that authorities may step into the market again.

item.title: Japan Confirms Three-Day Yen Intervention in Spring to Lift Yen
item.description: Japan said it intervened in the currency market three times during the spring Golden Week holiday to prop up the yen, going beyond its recent twin-punch playbook with an additional round in an apparent effort to maximize the psychological impact on investors.

item.title: Gold Steady as Traders Assess Impact of Hormuz Flare-Up on Rates
item.description: Gold moved in a narrow range as traders assessed the impact of a reported Iranian attack in the Strait of Hormuz on the Federal Reserve’s path for interest rates.

item.title: Japan’s Households Continue to Cut Spending Despite Wage Gains
item.description: Japan’s household spending unexpectedly fell for a seventh month even as real wages continued to increase, reflecting the impact of persistent inflation on consumer sentiment.

item.title: Atlassian Shares Surge as Revenue Jump Douses AI Fears
item.description: Atlassian Corp. shares surged in after-hours trading after quarterly revenue climbed, easing concerns that the software services company would be overtaken by artificial intelligence applications.

item.title: Chinese Banks Expand Direct Settlement to Aid Yuan’s Global Role
item.description: China is accelerating its push to internationalize the yuan as domestic banks add new foreign currencies available for direct settlement to bypass the dollar in cross-border trade.

item.title: Japan Sees Rush for Covenant Shelter as BBB-Rated Bond Sales Fly
item.description: Japanese companies have already sold more corporate bonds with investor protection this year than in all of 2025, as lower-rated borrowers increasingly turn to the bond market instead of relying solely on bank loans for their funding needs.

item.title: Japan Small Caps Face Survival Race as Topix Cull Looms
item.description: Japan’s Topix stock index is poised for its biggest overhaul, with more than 600 companies — over a third of its constituents — likely to be gradually removed under new eligibility rules, according to analysts’ estimates.

item.title: Oil Gains, Treasuries Hold Losses Before Jobs Data: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil rose as prospects for a lasting agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained elusive. Treasuries held their losses ahead of the key US jobs data report.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 7
item.description: Oil extended gains after a report that Iran attacked “hostile targets” in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran seeking to bar US ships from the critical waterway in a deal with Oman.

item.title: Fed’s Musalem Calls for Meaningful Restraint on Inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem said that with inflation running above the central bank’s 2% target, policymakers cannot afford to tolerate higher inflation while they wait for the possibility of stronger productivity growth.

item.title: North Korea's Kim Jong Un Gains $22 Billion Windfall Despite Sanctions
item.description: Trade records and satellite photos show how North Korea's dictator found new cash to fortify his nuclear arsenal.

item.title: Google’s Shakeup Complicates Race With OpenAI, Anthropic
item.description: The tech giant is entering a new period of transition.

item.title: Japan’s Carmakers Forecast Yen Staying Weak Despite US Intervention
item.description: Japan’s carmakers are assuming that the yen will trade near current levels against the US dollar in the coming months, based on forecasts they issued just as the US stepped in to help the Japanese currency from weakening further.
